new AXEClient(manifestDoc, options?): AXEClient;

Build a client from a manifest. Credentials are anchored at the origin discover() found the manifest on, or, for a manifest you obtained yourself, at its baseUrl origin: the client trusts a manifest you hand it. Add origins with trust.origins.

refresh()
refresh(options?): Promise<ManifestChange>;

Fetch the manifest again, conditionally (If-None-Match when the site sent an ETag), and replace this client's copy when it changed. Concurrent calls share one request. The new manifest's baseUrl must pass the destination policy, or the old manifest is kept and AXETrustError is thrown. Listeners from onManifestChange hear about a change.

run()
run<O>(
   name, 
   input, 
   options?
): Promise<RunOutcome<O>>;

Drive the whole escalation ladder: invoke, satisfy each needs_input from registered fulfillers (confirming sensitive payloads), poll pending work, and surface a handoff only when nothing else works.

When expectedRev is passed, the revision is tracked through the ladder: the first call carries it, and each continuation carries the rev of the result it continues from, so a change by someone else between two rungs is caught as conflict rather than applied blind.

stackTraceLimit
static stackTraceLimit: number;

The Error.stackTraceLimit property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by new Error().stack or Error.captureStackTrace(obj)).

The default value is 10 but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes will affect any stack trace captured after the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will not capture any frames.

Inherited from
Error.stackTraceLimit

Methods

captureStackTrace()
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;

Creates a .stack property on targetObject, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which Error.captureStackTrace() was called.

const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with ${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}.

The optional constructorOpt argument accepts a function. If given, all frames above constructorOpt, including constructorOpt, will be omitted from the generated stack trace.

The constructorOpt argument is useful for hiding implementation details of error generation from the user. For instance:

function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();

manifestMaxAgeMs?
optional manifestMaxAgeMs?: number;

Longest time, in ms, a fetched manifest is used before ensureFresh() revalidates it. The effective bound is the smaller of this and the manifest response's Cache-Control max-age (no-cache and no-store mean 0). Default 300000. See "Manifest freshness".

maxResponseBytes?
optional maxResponseBytes?: number;

Largest response body the client reads, in bytes. A larger Content-Length is refused before reading; a body without one is read up to the limit, then cancelled. Default 4194304 (4 MiB).

maxRetryAfterMs?

Longest Retry-After the client will honor automatically, in ms. Default 30000.

TrustOptions

Where the client may send requests and credentials. The anchor is the origin you discovered from (discover(url), AXEClient.discover(url)), or the baseUrl origin of a manifest you hand to new AXEClient yourself. The credential audience is the anchor plus origins.

Properties

allowCrossOrigin?
optional allowCrossOrigin?: boolean;

Contact other https origins named by the site (baseUrl, live.url, pollUrl, discovery hints), without auth or headers. Loopback and private-range host names stay refused. Default false.

allowHttp?
optional allowHttp?: boolean | "localhost";

Plain http. "localhost" (default): only for localhost, 127.x.x.x, and [::1] origins in the credential audience. false: https everywhere. true: http anywhere (a private network you control). An https-to-http redirect is refused whatever this says.

destinationPolicy?
optional destinationPolicy?: (request) => MaybePromise<boolean>;

Called for every outbound URL, redirects included, after the built-in checks pass. Return false to refuse. Use it to bind the client to your own network policy. It sees URLs, not resolved addresses: it does not stop DNS rebinding. See docs/security.md.

Parameters
request

DestinationRequest

Returns

MaybePromise<boolean>

origins?
optional origins?: string[];

More origins (https://api.example; a path is ignored) that may be contacted with credentials: a manifest baseUrl, live.url, pollUrl, or discovery hint on another origin.

Functions

discover()

function discover(url, options?): Promise<{
  manifest: Manifest;
  manifestUrl: string;
  via: "well-known" | "alias" | "header" | "link";
}>;

Find a manifest starting from any URL: /.well-known/axe.json, /axe/manifest, the AXE-Manifest response header, then a <link rel="axe-manifest"> in the page. Returns the manifest and where it was found. A hint or redirect to another origin is followed only when trust authorizes it. The returned manifest remembers the discovery origin, so new AXEClient(manifest) anchors its credentials there, not at the manifest's baseUrl.
